correctness.rationale: For every \(B>0\), the exact six-pair connectivity polynomial follows by summing three one-edge, two two-edge, and one three-edge path products under independent edge successes. At fixed center investment and outer total, AM--GM strictly forces equality of outer investments, including the zero-outer-budget boundary. The resulting one-variable derivative has the sign of \(R-H(u)\), where \(H(u)=u^3(3-u)/[2(2-u)]\) increases strictly on \((0,1]\), and \(H(\sqrt R)<R<H(1)\), so exactly one positive interior global maximum exists. The center premium and its strict monotonicity follow by algebra and inversion of \(H\); small- and large-budget expansions use \(H^{\prime}(1)=7/2\) and \(H(u)\sim3u^3/4\). Three patches have the strict AM--GM equal optimum; two patches are trivial. The checker passed 40,071 supplementary assertions, including separate eight-state enumeration; the analytic arguments prove the continuum statement.

value.rationale: The objective is the established all-pairs ecological connectivity surrogate, and four equal-value patches are the first natural path length allowing a strict center-edge priority over uniform expenditure. The theorem classifies the complete allocation globally at every \(B>0\), not just a numerical example: both outer edges remain equal and positive, the center is always preferred, the extra center investment is bounded by the sharp absolute constant \(\log(4/3)\), and small- and large-budget shares are explicit. These are meaningful benchmarks distinguishing pair-connectivity optimization from serial-system reliability and discrete restoration heuristics. No unsupported field-efficacy claim is made.
